bullets.title: Brent crude hits $100-$101/bbl on Iran-Houthi escalation; multi-asset selloff ensues
bullets.body: Brent crude surged above $100/bbl for the first time since May—touching $101—driven by Strait of Hormuz closure, drone attacks on oil tankers near the Caspian Pipeline, and Trump signaling a 'massive attack' on Iran. The cross-asset impact was severe: stocks, bonds, crypto, and gold all sold off simultaneously while energy rallied. Crack spreads collapsed as refiner margins compressed under the crude spike.

bullets.title: Fed rate hike odds spike to 36-72%; 10Y yield breaks 4.70% to new 52-week high
bullets.body: CME FedWatch probability of a rate hike jumped from 12% to 36% in a single week, while separate market estimates show 72% cumulative probability of a hike before year-end—both cycle highs. The US 10-year yield broke above 4.70% for the first time since January, surpassing the 'Liberation Day' high from April. At the same time, the 30-year fixed mortgage rate hit 6.85% (Freddie Mac) and 6.58% in the same week—highest since August 2025—tightening financial conditions further.

bullets.title: ECB holds at 2.25%; Lagarde warns full energy shock 'yet to play out,' flags upside inflation risks
bullets.body: ECB left all three rates unchanged as expected (deposit at 2.25%, MRO at 2.40%, marginal lending at 2.65%) and committed to a data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach with no forward guidance. Lagarde explicitly stated risks to inflation are tilted to the upside and risks to growth tilted to the downside, and that the full inflationary impact of the energy shock has not yet materialized. She asked staff to model oil/gas price scenarios for the September meeting, and flagged that energy will keep Eurozone inflation above target through H1 2027.

bullets.title: Magnificent 7 on pace for worst day since April 2025; Nasdaq -2%, S&P -1.3%
bullets.body: The Mag 7 index was tracking its worst single session since April 2025, with GOOGL down ~7.6% (second-largest earnings-day decline in company history), TSLA down 14.1% (second-worst earnings reaction ever), and the Nasdaq 100 off 2% while the S&P fell 1.3%. The SPY showed a $3.3B put wall at the 740 strike as the key support level for bulls, while VIX hit one-month highs post-OPEX.

bullets.title: Jobless claims plunge to 187k—lowest since 1969—contradicting labor market fears
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 187k vs. 210k estimate and 209k prior, the lowest level since 1969. Continuing claims came in at 1.796M vs. 1.809M estimate. The data lands against a backdrop of rising rate hike expectations and was met with a market-wide sell-off driven by oil and geopolitics rather than labor concerns.

bullets.title: Kansas City Fed manufacturing misses; employment index drops sharply
bullets.body: Kansas City Fed manufacturing activity came in at 9 vs. 12 estimated and 11 prior. New orders fell to 10 from 13, employment dropped sharply to 2 from 10, and prices paid declined to 52 from 68—suggesting some moderation in input cost pressures even as output holds up.

bullets.title: AAII bullish sentiment crashes 15+ pts to 29.6%—lowest since September
bullets.body: AAII investor sentiment fell more than 15 percentage points this week to 29.6%, below the 30% threshold and the lowest reading since September. The sharp sentiment deterioration aligns with the concurrent market selloff driven by oil, rates, and big-cap earnings disappointments.

bullets.title: Google Q2: record $112B net income but 87% from equity gains; FCF turns negative for first time
bullets.body: Alphabet's headline Q2 net income of $112B was record-setting but misleading—87% stemmed from equity investment markups (SpaceX, Anthropic), leaving core earnings up only ~2% QoQ. More critically, Google posted -$5.9B in free cash flow, the first quarterly negative FCF in its public history, as capex surged to $44.9B per quarter and full-year guidance was raised to $195-205B (from $180-190B). Contracted future spending commitments ballooned to $811B as of June 30—up ~$500B in three months. Shares fell 5.8-7.6%.

bullets.title: Gold overtakes US Treasuries in central bank FX reserves; gold down ~2% on session
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported that gold has surpassed US Treasuries as the largest component of central bank foreign exchange reserves—a significant structural shift. Despite the longer-term bullish reserve trend, spot gold fell ~2% on the day to $4,046/oz as risk-off flows were dominated by oil and rates volatility rather than safe-haven buying.

bullets.title: US-Iran: Senate blocks war powers resolution 47-49; House passes 214-208; military escalation risk high
bullets.body: The Senate voted 47-49 to kill a war powers resolution aimed at ending Trump's Iran hostilities, while the House passed its own resolution 214-208. Iran's Navy says the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, the IRGC declared any base used to attack Iran a legitimate target, and explosions were reported on Qeshm and Larak Islands. Trump told Axios he is 'seriously considering restarting major combat operations.' ECB's Lagarde said the Middle East situation 'can reverse very quickly.'

bullets.title: USTR global tariff announcement flagged; EU-US trade tensions escalate
bullets.body: White House press secretary Leavitt signaled a USTR tariff announcement later in the session on global tariffs. Separately, USTR Greer stated EU actions are 'driving massive uncertainty for US exports' and continue targeting competitive US companies. The EU passed its 21st sanctions package against Russia via written procedure.

bullets.title: AMD Advancing AI Day: Lisa Su pegs AI accelerator TAM at $1.4T by 2030; CPU TAM expands to $220B
bullets.body: AMD CEO Lisa Su delivered sweeping TAM expansion claims: AI accelerator market seen reaching $1.4T by 2030 (comparable to the entire semiconductor market today), overall compute market $2T by 2030, and the server/agentic CPU TAM growing from $60B to $120B to $220B as billions of AI agents drive core demand. Su noted 2026 marks the first year inference compute exceeds training compute globally. Venice EPYC is in full production with a claimed 20% performance lead over NVIDIA CPUs, with systems shipping in Q4.

bullets.title: AMD partners Cerebras for ultra-low-latency inference; NVDA acquires Groq—inference race intensifies
bullets.body: AMD announced a partnership with Cerebras combining the Helios GPU rack with Cerebras's wafer-scale chip for AI inference, launching on Cerebras Cloud in H2 2026. Simultaneously, NVIDIA is reportedly acquiring Groq. OpenAI's infrastructure chief confirmed plans to work with AMD on the MI500 series and is already using Helios racks. Anthropic confirmed Claude bootstraps on AMD Instinct + ROCm, seen as evidence that NVIDIA's CUDA moat is eroding. One analyst flagged that AMD's CPU TAM came in below BofA desk numbers, tempering enthusiasm.

bullets.title: Fitch: US credit outlook increasingly dependent on sustained AI investment confidence
bullets.body: Fitch warned that the US credit outlook is now materially tied to sustained confidence in AI investment, with widening disparities in AI-related capex across companies and sectors becoming a key credit driver. Separately, a bearish critique flagged that $2T in 'circular AI financing' is contingent on Anthropic/OpenAI monetizing $1.5T+ in unfunded commitments—which may not prove feasible given Chinese open-source LLM competition.

bullets.title: Tesla Q2: record $28B revenue +26% YoY but margins collapse; stock down 14.1%—2nd worst earnings day ever
bullets.body: Tesla posted Q2 revenue of $28B (+26% YoY, strongest since Q2 2023) and deliveries of 480k (+25% YoY), but net income fell 5% to $1.1B and operating margins collapsed to 1.4% from 4.1% YoY. The stock fell 14.1%, its second-worst earnings reaction in company history (only the Nov. 2013 reaction was worse). Bears note ~88% of revenue remains automotive, Samsung's market cap has overtaken Tesla's, and management failed to disclose metrics on unsupervised autonomous vehicle operations.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex ROI framing: 2024 spend driving current earnings; FCF decline may pressure rates
bullets.body: Bulls defend Google's capex surge by pointing to historical patterns where large capex investments at AMZN, MSFT, and GOOGL drove revenue 1-2 years later. However, a bearish read notes declining hyperscaler free cash flow as an underrated factor weighing on bond markets and potentially driving forward rates higher—creating a feedback loop between AI capex and rates volatility.

bullets.title: Big Tech off-balance-sheet liabilities: $1.65T for GOOGL/MSFT/AMZN/META/ORCL—up 8x in 4 years
bullets.body: A Nikkei study cited on social media found that off-balance-sheet obligations for Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle have grown 8x over four years to $1.65T—liabilities that don't appear on standard balance sheets. The figure adds to concerns about the true leverage embedded in large-cap tech at a time when rates are rising sharply.

bullets.title: Iran commodity price cascade: crude +35%, European nat gas +94%, jet fuel +46% since conflict onset
bullets.body: Since the onset of the Iran conflict, a broad commodity price cascade has unfolded: sulfur +146%, European natural gas +94%, heating oil +64%, jet fuel +46%, diesel +39%, gasoline +37%, rice +37%, WTI/Brent crude each +35%, wheat +20%. These moves are beginning to feed through to mortgage rates (6.85%, highest of 2026) and ECB inflation projections. Oil vol is also perpetuating rates vol in a self-reinforcing loop.

bullets.title: Intel and AMD lock Chinese cloud firms into year-long CPU deals amid 40% price surge
bullets.body: Intel and AMD are securing year-long CPU supply agreements with Chinese cloud companies, with CPU prices reportedly up 40% amid supply tightness. The deals provide revenue visibility for both chipmakers even as geopolitical pressures intensify around the broader tech supply chain.

bullets.title: Bipartisan AI 'kill switch' bill introduced; New York data center moratorium persists
bullets.body: Representatives Obernolte (R) and Trahan (D) introduced bipartisan legislation that would grant the government power to restrict AI models presenting catastrophic risks. Separately, New York Governor Hochul defended her AI data center construction moratorium amid industry criticism, while the Trump administration announced a 'Ratepayer Protection Pledge' to prevent data center infrastructure costs from raising consumer utility prices.
